References particularly useful for this section

Deshpande, S., Thottan, M., Ho, T. K., & Sikdar, B. (2009). An Online Mechanism for BGP Instability Detection and Analysis. IEEE Transactions on Computers, 58(11), 1470–1484. The paper explicitly states that its BGP features were collected at five-minute intervals.

Fonseca, P., Mota, E., Bennesby, R., & Passito, A. (2019). BGP Dataset Generation and Feature Extraction for Anomaly Detection. 2019 IEEE Symposium on Computers and Communications (ISCC). DOI: 10.1109/ISCC47284.2019.8969619. The authors explicitly generated datasets at 1-, 5-, and 10-minute timescales.

I would cite both in the dissertation. Deshpande et al. gives you a strong historical precedent for specifically using five-minute BGP feature intervals, while Fonseca et al. is particularly valuable because it directly connects BGP feature engineering + temporal bins + machine-learning dataset construction, which is very close to your methodology.
